reviews.comment: Lectures are helpful but not required, lecture notes are provided for the entire semester. Two exams, both open note. Weekly homework and exam problems are reused from previous years. Practice exams are not provided but past exams are available on his website.
reviews.ratingTags: Clear grading criteria--Graded by few things

reviews.comment: Super duper easy, final is open computer. Go to lecture be neat and meticulous in homework and midterm. Very accessible outside of class. Really truly wants to see kids want to learn and love physics
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Graded by few things--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Class was pretty easy for the most part. First half of the class is learning new ways to solve mechanics problems, and the other half is E&M and Quantum Physics. Homeworks are initially easy but do get harder as you continue through the course. Midterm is take home, and final is everything open note. Review old exam problems before the test.

Abanov makes one of the most difficult classes to take as an engineer that much more manageable. There's no skirting around the difficulty of the content, and grading is harsh, but he is incredibly fair in his assessment - I never felt like it was someone else's fault I did not do well on a question. The 5-point extra credit questions were great.

Artem makes it VERY clear that learning is more important than grades. HWs are difficult and graded strictly, 1st exam is a take-home exam, 2nd exam is everything open-note, and he offers you 5+ points on your ENTIRE grade for each of the 3 extra problems you manage to proof and solve. His lectures are very interesting and engaging. Awesome prof!

I sat in on this course after taking a similar course some years ago.  This course was much better and deeper than my previous course.  At the end of the course, Abanov presented material that would not be on the Final that was profound: showing how Classical Mechanics could be derived from Quantum Mechanics and not the other way around.

Abanov isn't a bad guy but he is not a great lecturer. He can be helpful when asking questions about hw. The hws got progressively more difficult mainly because the last few chapters were difficult. Exams are similar to homework and past exams. Extra credit is hard to do but worth the effort. He grades tough so be thorough on work. Def take him!GL!

Dr. Abanov is without a doubt one of the smartest individuals I have ever met. No joke I think this guy knows everything. That being said his lecture material is EXTREMELY difficult I could never keep up with what he was talking about. That being said though he repeats questions from previous exams which is why everyone does so well 10/10
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He is a pretty solid professor for PHYS-222. He makes lectures engaging, and is just an overall chill prof. Make sure you study previous tests before the exams, and understand the homeworks too.

Abanov knows the subject well. He treats the class like a graduate level course, which definitely adds to the difficulty but some find this more enjoyable. Majority of the grade is homework, which are 3-5 difficult questions. Good professor!

My grade consisted of two tests and homework. Homework everyone just cheggs as they are really hard to do without it but actually understand it as he will take off points if you don't understand it. The tests are pretty hard if you are unprepared so do the problems from his old homeworks and tests as my tests questions came from there.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough Grader--GRADED BY FEW THINGS--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: Great professor. Lectures are interesting, his accent is fun. Gives extra credit if you can solve some difficult problems.
reviews.ratingTags: Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He can be kinda scary at first, but he's helpful as anything if you ask for it. He's also quite responsive in lecture. And the Russian accent is fun, he knows what he needs to say in English, even if sometimes it takes a while to say.

Great professor. Very clear in what he is explaining (uses the board tons for pictures to help you out, doesn't go too fast if people are confused). Accent not bad. Shows real physics behind equations for those who care. Grades on a curve. Always open to questions and willing to help. Has some sense of humor to keep you from being completely bored.
